mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity cash flows and stimulate economic activity through cheaper borrowing.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) within the last month signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: High GDP growth (GDPC1 > 11000.0) combined with strong housing starts (HOUST > 2200.0) indicates late-cycle expansion where inflation and rate hikes suppress equity returns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 > 11000.0 and HOUST > 2200.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST < 2000.0) signals weakening real estate activity that reduces consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 2000.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) and stable monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) signal persistent inflation that triggers rate hikes, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained employment growth (PAYEMS > 132000.0) over three months indicates strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 132000.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 115.0) signals manufacturing contraction and supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 115.0.
